We need respond with JSON only. Need evaluate each 69 stories for Unambiguous. Need be careful. Criterion: avoids terms/abstractions leading to multiple materially different interpretations. Violation when vague, underspecified, overloaded, unclear terms allow materially different requirements interpretations. Not harmless stylistic variation. Need evaluate each story. We can decide per story. Need use full backlog maybe for context but individual scope. Need identify vague terms. Many stories have typos, grammar errors but not necessarily unambiguous if meaning still clear? We should focus material ambiguity. Need return exactly one object per story ID. No prose.

Need go through all 69. I'll list decisions. Need concise evidence/rationale. Confidence. Related empty for individual. Let's reason each.

BC-001: "As a anonymoususer, I want to view a list of sponsors, so that I can thank all the awesome sponsors." Ambiguous? "list of sponsors" clear enough. "thank" not specified? It's rationale. Maybe no material ambiguity. No violation.

BC-002: view list of user profiles, "so that I know who is attending conference." Clear. No violation.

BC-003: "As a trainingcoordinator, I want to email all the trainers at once from the website for info and updates, so that It is easier to use." "email all trainers at once from website" clear? Slight grammar. No material ambiguity. No violation.

BC-004: "As a attendee, I want to have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are, so that I can make it to class on time." "very clear map" vague? "very clear" is subjective but not materially different requirement? Could mean visual clarity, but likely not ambiguous in software terms? Hmm criterion: vague terms allow materially different interpretations. "very clear map" maybe subjective but not multiple requirements? It could mean detailed map or easy-to-read. But story is about map where buildings and rooms are. Maybe no violation. I'd say no.

BC-005: "As a trainer, I want to edit my training node myself, so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides." "edit my training node" maybe clear in Drupal context. "links to slides" appended unclear. Could be ambiguous: wants to edit training node and links to slides? Evidence "links to slides" is unclear. Does it mean include links to slides? Does this allow multiple interpretations? Maybe yes. The story is confused: "so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides." The "and links to slides" unclear. Violation.

BC-006: "As a trainee, I want to limit to one registration per day per authenticated user, so that we don't have duplicate spaces." Clear rule. No violation.

BC-007: "As a trainingcoordinator, I want to have an admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee so that, so that we can see if attendend, refunded, no show." Term "registration status" maybe clear with attendend typo, refunded, no show. No material ambiguity? "attendend" typo means attended. no violation maybe. Could be "status" clear. No.

BC-008: "As a attendee, I want to be added to a training waitlist, so that so they can be considered for a class." Clear. "they" pronoun mismatch but not ambiguous requirement. No.

BC-009: "As a trainee, I want to must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox, so that they can be accountable.." Clear. No violation.

BC-010: "As a trainingcoordinator, I want to tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists, so that so we don't loose money or spots." "whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists" vague: doesn't specify. Could be materially ambiguous. Also "tie in" vague. Violation likely.

BC-011: "As a trainee, I want to add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site, so that they can schedule their event experience." Conditional "if there is a schedule feature" unclear whether required? But statement says wants to add to my schedule if feature exists, vague. Also "my schedule" maybe ambiguous. Violation? I'd say yes because conditional and unknown "my schedule" not defined. But maybe "add to my schedule" clear. However "if there is a schedule feature on the site" introduces uncertainty. Could lead materially different interpretation: implement schedule feature? Or only integrate if exists? Violation.

BC-012: "As a trainee, I want to see which trainings I have signed up for, so that they can schedule their event experience." Clear. No violation.

BC-013: "As a trainer, I want to have a view that is attached to their training node that shows all attendee information Trainers can see all class attendance at first because there are so little trainers and they are trusted with privacy, so that the training coordinator doesn't have to do all the work to get login info for environment setup." Long, "all attendee information" broad/underspecified: what attendee info? "Trainers can see all class attendance at first..." ambiguous. Violation.

BC-014: "As a trainingcoordinator, I want to have an admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session, so that I can see WTF is happening." "all trainee information" broad/underspecified. Violation. Evidence "all trainee information".

BC-015: "As a anonymoususer, I want to have a dedicated page for each class to learn more about the offering The following information must be shown: Logo, title, trainers, location, possibly a map view, datetime, skill level, registrations remaining, link to register for class. The URL path should be SEO friendly /training/training-title, so that I can choose the right class, AND the trainer can tweet and promote their class." Quite detailed. "possibly a map view" ambiguous? It says possibly; not mandatory. Could be interpreted optional. But not materially different? Might be a requirement uncertainty. "Logo, title..." clear. "SEO friendly" maybe subjective but standard. No violation? "possibly a map view" is vague whether required. Hmm. Could violate because ambiguous requirement whether map view is required. But maybe not central? Let's decide maybe No Violation because specifics are clear despite optional map. Need not over-flag. But "possibly a map view" means maybe yes/no, materially different scope.
